issue: Theorem 7.10(iv) says 'the parameter never exceeds the one obtained by keeping the private variables as ordinary coordinates'. The proof compares only the Euclidean numbers kappa(L^+,g_V) and kappa(L_F,g_F). The approximation theorem for the problem with the private variables kept (Thm 5.9(b)) uses the weighted kappa-bar, which can be much smaller. Theorems 7.2(b) and 7.10(iii) are stated only with the Euclidean kappa_V.
evidence: Take r=0 (or a block that does not couple) and F_0(v)=100 v_1^2+v_2^2 on [-1,1]^2. Then L^+=200, g=1, kappa_V=200, so Thm 7.10(iii) gives f(p,200)200^C(I+q+1)^C. But F=(1/2)(200v_1^2+2v_2^2) has weighted growth with gamma=1/2, so kappa-bar=2, and Thm 5.9(b) gives f(p,2)(I+q+1)^5. The stronger statement is true. If F-OPT >= gamma sum L_i^F (x_i-x_i^*)^2 and L_i^+ <= max{(H_0)_ii,0}=L_i^F, then V(v)-OPT=F(v,y(v))-OPT >= gamma sum_{i in K} L_i^+ (v_i-v_i^*)^2, so kappa-bar_V <= kappa-bar_F. App. C.1(b) already uses only weighted growth of V.
fix: Replace the second sentence of (iv) with: 'Thus kappa(L^+,g) never exceeds the Euclidean condition number kappa(L,g) of F with the private variables kept as ordinary coordinates.' Optional strengthening: state Thm 7.2(b) and Thm 7.10(iii) under weighted growth of V with kappa-bar_V, and add to (iv): 'and V inherits weighted growth from F with kappa-bar_V <= kappa-bar_F, because L_i^+ <= L_i^F.'

issue: The sentence 'Section 7.3 evaluates V exactly and bounds its curvature by quantities that do not see such stiff convex terms' overstates what Section 7.3 achieves. The paper's own Remark C.11 and Proposition 7.13 show that the certified curvature can keep the full stiffness.
evidence: Remark C.11: for M(y-w)^2+eps y with eps>0, the short clipped piece forces sigma=0, and the value has second derivative 2M. Proposition 7.13: L_K/g_K >= M for every admissible K, while nu/g <= 4.
fix: Replace with: 'Section 7.3 evaluates V exactly and certifies curvature bounds that can cancel such stiff convex terms (Theorem 7.10), though not always (Proposition 7.13);'. Optionally, in recourse-convex.tex:5-6, change 'depends only on the coordinate curvature of the reduced objective' to 'depends only on the coordinate curvature and the growth of the reduced objective'.

issue: The title 'Local corrections need exact recourse' claims a necessity that is not proved. Theorem 7.4 shows that certified approximate recourse also suffices (eps_or > 0 is allowed). Proposition C.1 allows uncertified values whose error varies little over the corners. Proposition 7.5 refutes only one alternative: grid min-marginals with a constant allowance.
evidence: Thm 7.4 hypotheses (eq:cr-oracle) allow eps_or > 0; Prop C.1 allows values with bounded error oscillation; Prop 7.5 concerns only the constant-correction test with grid min-marginals. The w2 review (R2 m8) removed the same necessity claim from the body text, but the title still makes it.
fix: Retitle: 'Bag-local corrections and conditional recourse' (or 'Local corrections with exact or certified recourse').

issue: The exact procedure of Theorem 7.10(iii) has no termination guarantee without point growth, and the text does not say so. Theorem 6.14 (EX) and Theorem 7.2(c) do stop on every instance, and the results table lists Theorem 7.10 next to them, so a reader may assume the same here.
evidence: The procedure rounds each continuous retained coordinate of the incumbent to a rational with denominator at most Lambda_0. Without uniqueness, the incumbents may approach a continuum of minimizers whose points have larger denominators, so the acceptance test may never pass. REC is not available because the slices are polytopes (w3 F67). The theorem itself claims a bound only under growth and validity without growth, so no stated claim is false.
fix: After 'valid without growth or uniqueness' in (iii), add: 'Without point growth of F the exact procedure is not guaranteed to stop; if every Y_t is a box, Theorem 7.2(c) applies instead and EX stops on every instance.'
